rows.quote: Upon identification of potential duplicates, a manual confirmation will always be necessary. Those transmitted ICSRs should be complete, entire and undiminished in their structure, format and content. Registration holders could also collaborate with NPC in the detection of duplicate reports. If there is conflicting or limited information, which on the first review does not allow the determination that the cases are duplicates, additional information from the reporter or sender needs to be sought.

f.title: Significant safety issues requiring prompt communication to NPC (items a-h)
f.statement: Significant safety issues require prompt communication to NPC and include, among others: (a) safety-driven modification or removal of an indication; (b) a new contraindication; (c) major changes to warnings, precautions or ADR statements in any country; (d) withdrawal or suspension in another country; (e) issues from the holder’s own signal management once assessed and actions proposed; (f) significant safety results from post-marketing clinical studies; (g) misinformation in product information; (h) use outside the product information.

f.statement: Registration holders’ press releases should refer to the regulatory action taken by DRAP, and relevant ongoing reviews should be mentioned in any registration holder communication.
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: Their press releases should refer to the regulatory action taken by the DRAP. Relevant ongoing reviews should be mentioned in any communication by the registration holders.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: press release content (should). Double-check: confirmed; below 90: 'Their press releases' refers back to the registration holders in the preceding sentence.

f.title: Keep website safety information accessible and understandable
f.statement: NPC-DRAP and registration holders should ensure that important safety information on websites they control is easily accessible and understandable by the public (and kept up to date, with outdated information marked or removed).
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: NPC-DRAP as well as registration holders of therapeutic goods should ensure that important safety information published on websites under their control is easily accessible and understandable by the public.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: websites. The next sentence ('kept up-to-date ... out-of-' / 'date') contains a line-end hyphen and is not quoted. Double-check: confirmed: NPC-DRAP and holders named with 'should ensure'; below 90: the up-to-date/outdated clause in the statement is not quoted (line-end hyphen).

f.title: Ensure accuracy when using social media for safety information
f.statement: Safety information may be disseminated via social media and other web tools; when using such rapid channels, special attention should be paid to ensuring the accuracy of the information is not compromised.
f.clause: 9.5.5 Social media and other online communications
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: Online safety information may also be disseminated via social media platforms such as Facebook, Twitter and LinkedIn and other web tools. When using newer, more rapid communication channels, special attention should be paid to ensure that the accuracy of the information released is not compromised
rows.location: 9.5.5 Social media and other online communications
rows.review_note: Review: new row: social media. Mixed may/should; Recommended for the accuracy expectation. Double-check: confirmed; below 90: mixed 'may'/'should'; passive.

f.title: NPC-DRAP informs provincial PV centres of national regulatory actions
f.statement: NPC-DRAP shall inform the provincial pharmacovigilance centres in a timely manner about national regulatory actions taken on a new safety concern.
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: NPC-DRAP shall inform the provincial pharmacovigilance centres in a timely manner about the regulatory actions taken at the level of national level with regards to the new safety concern.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: NPC duty (authority actor). Double-check: below 90: authority-only row (duty of DRAP/NPC, no registration-holder step); kept for context but not for auto-publication.

f.title: Have systems to respond to public enquiries consistent with DRAP recommendations
f.statement: DRAP and registration holders should have systems to respond to enquiries from members of the public; responses should reflect public-domain information and DRAP’s recommendations, and patients asking for individual treatment advice should be referred to an HCP.
f.clause: 9.5.10 Responding to enquiries from the public
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: DRAP and registration holders should have systems in place for responding to enquiries about therapeutic goods from individual members of the public. In Pakistan, there is the Pakistan Citizen Portal mobile application where the public can complain about public offices on any matter of their daily life including the matters related to therapeutic goods. Responses should take into account the information which is in the public domain and should include the relevant recommendations to patients and healthcare professionals issued by DRAP. Where questions relate to individual treatment advice, the patient should be advised to contact a healthcare professional.
rows.location: 9.5.10 Responding to enquiries from the public
rows.review_note: Review: new row: enquiries from the public. Double-check: confirmed: DRAP and holders 'should have systems in place'; below 90: shared actor and the HCP-referral sentence is passive.

f.title: Keep purchase, import, production, distribution and sale records for controlled drugs
f.statement: For controlled drugs (narcotics, psychotropics, precursors), records of purchase, import, dispensing, production, distribution and sale are to be kept at all levels and may be requested by the regulator at any time.
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)
f.processes: Data integrity & records; Risk management & minimisation

rows.quote: The records of purchase, import, dispensing, production, distribution and sale are to be kept at all levels and may be asked by the regulator at any time to avoid their misuse.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: record keeping for controlled drugs ('are to be kept' = Mandatory). Applies at all levels of the supply chain, including the registration holder (manufacture, import, distribution). Double-check: scrutinised: the sentence sits in the description of the controlled-drug legal-status regime (narcotics/psychotropics quota) and says records 'are to be kept at all levels'; it is passive with no named duty-bearer, outside core PV, and reads as a description of the national controlled-drug regime rather than a GVP duty of this guideline. Kept for admin review; Mandatory is a judgement call.

f.title: Prioritise safety concerns and introduce aRMM only when essential
f.statement: When additional risk minimisation is needed, safety concerns are to be prioritised by frequency, seriousness, severity, public health impact and preventability; whether routine measures suffice is to be considered first; and additional measures should only be introduced when essential for safe and effective use and be developed and provided by suitably qualified people.
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: When additional risk minimisation activities are needed, safety concerns are to be prioritised in terms of frequency, seriousness, severity, impact on public health and preventability. Likewise, careful consideration is then to be given to whether the goal/aim can be reached with routine minimisation activities, and, if not considered sufficient, which additional minimisation measure(s) is (are) will be the most appropriate. Additional risk minimisation activities/measures should only be introduced when they are deemed to be essential for the safe and effective use of the medicinal product and should be developed and provided by suitably qualified people.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: additional risk minimisation ('are to be' / 'should'). Double-check: confirmed; below 90: 'are to be prioritised/considered' and 'should' mixed under Recommended; actor inferred.

f.title: Educational material focuses on actionable risk-minimisation messages
f.statement: Any educational material should focus on actionable goals and give clear, concise messages on actions to prevent and minimise selected risks.
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: Any educational material should focus on actionable goals and should provide clear and concise messages describing actions to be taken in order to prevent and minimise selected risks.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: educational material focus. Quote starts after a page footer. Double-check: confirmed; below 90: passive wording; the registration holder actor is inferred, not named in the quote; quote follows a page footer.

f.title: Provide educational materials in accessible formats and user-test them
f.statement: Educational materials should ideally be available in a range of formats so access is not limited by disability or internet access, and where feasible the tool and media should be user-tested with the target audience in advance.
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: Ideally, educational materials should be available in a range of formats to ensure that access is not limited by disability or access to the internet. When feasible the appropriateness of the tool and media for the target audience (e.g. suitable language, pictures, diagrams, or other graphical support) should be user tested in advance, in order to optimise the success of the implementation phase.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: 10.4.1. Double-check: confirmed; below 90: passive wording; the registration holder actor is inferred, not named in the quote.

f.title: Keep educational programmes separate from promotion and aligned with the SmPC/PL
f.statement: Educational programmes should be completely separate from promotion; contact information gathered should not be used for promotion; content should be aligned with and add to (not duplicate) the SmPC and PL; promotional elements should not be included; and the focus should be on the risks needing additional risk minimisation.
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: Any educational programme should be completely separated from promotional activities and contact information of physicians or patients gathered through educational programmes should not be used for promotional activities. The content of any educational material should be fully aligned with product information for a therapeutic good, such as the SmPC and PL, and should add rather than duplicate SmPC and PL information. Promotional elements, either direct or veiled (e.g. logos, product brand colours, suggestive images and pictures), should not be included and the focus of the educational material should be on the risk(s) related to the product and the management of those risk (s) requiring additional risk minimisation.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: 10.4.2. Double-check: confirmed; below 90: passive wording; the registration holder actor is inferred, not named in the quote.

f.title: Focus educational tools on RMP safety concerns and refer to the SmPC/PL
f.statement: Educational tools should focus on clearly defined actions for specific RMP safety concerns, avoid diluting content with ambiguous or irrelevant information already in the SmPC/PL, and refer the reader to the SmPC and package leaflet.
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: Should focus on clearly defined actions related to specific safety concerns described in the RMP and should not be unnecessarily diluted by including ambiguous statements (s) or such information that is not immediately relevant to the safety concern and that is already adequately presented in the SmPC or package leaflet. Educational tools should refer the reader to the information of SmPC and the package leaflet.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: 10.4.3. Double-check: confirmed; below 90: the first sentence starts 'Should focus' without its subject ('Educational tools'); passive.

f.title: Keep patient alert card content minimal and the card easy to carry
f.statement: Patient alert card information should be kept to the minimum needed to convey key minimisation messages and required mitigating action, including in an emergency, and the card should be easy to carry (e.g. wallet-sized).
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: The information should be kept to the minimum necessary in order to convey the key minimisation message(s) and the required mitigating action, in any circumstances, including an emergency. The ability to carry the patient alert card with ease (e.g. it can be fitted in a wallet) should be a key design feature of this tool.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: 10.4.6. Double-check: confirmed; below 90: 'The information' refers to the patient alert card named in the heading; passive.

f.title: Use controlled access only for important risks of clearly beneficial products
f.statement: Controlled access should only be considered to minimise an important risk with significant public health or patient impact for a product with clearly demonstrated benefits that would otherwise not be available, where access depends on meeting requirements before prescribing or dispensing.
f.applicability: Therapeutic goods registered in Pakistan (PHSR/GL/PV/07, Edition 01)

rows.quote: Therefore, controlled access should only be considered as a tool for minimising an important risk with significant public health or individual patient impact for a product with clearly demonstrated benefits but which would not otherwise be available without a programme where patient access is contingent on fulfilling one or more requirements prior to a product being prescribed or dispensed in order to assure its safe use.
rows.review_note: Review: new row: controlled access. The later 'measures should be put in place to ensure monitoring' sentence crosses a page footer and is not curated separately. Double-check: confirmed; below 90: passive wording; the registration holder actor is inferred, not named in the quote.
